newsitem.title: EGYPT: Dollar shortage pushes Egypt pound down.
newsitem.headline: Dollar shortage pushes Egypt pound down.

text.p: A dollar shortage in the private-sector market pushed the Egyptian pound down on Monday, bankers said.
Several bankers said many public sector banks were balancing their accounts before the end of the fiscal year and were borrowing dollars heavily. The year ends on June 30.
Others attributed the shortage to a lack of people willing to sell the U.S. currency. "The interbank rates are pretty high so they're holding onto their money," one banker said.
Private-sector bankers said the dollar ranged from 3.3940 pounds to 3.3970 pounds bid and from 3.3955 pounds to 3.3995 offered in the interbank market.
A survey of four actively trading banks gave average rates of 3.3950 pounds bid and 3.3974 pounds offered. The averages compare to 3.3943 bid and 3.3963 offered on Sunday.
The Central Bank calculated the average exchange rate at midday as 3.392033 buy and 3.398212 sell.
